proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the path-space tilt, the exact same-ledger reset and persistent-memory witnesses, the sharp worst-fiber order, and a matched sampling-versus-mesh frontier on a regular binary-bin subclass. D0.5 specialist reviews found no mathematical defect, but the general reviewer graded the scoped package at subfield, below the fixed field floor. A field-level successor would require a new program for full reset-class inference, individual fiber endpoints, matched no-reset upper theory, or a substantive application.
tldr: Under controlled finite-state reset, an observable \(g\)-recursion center has an explicit order-\(\delta\) outer radius for the continuous-time suppression mean. A split-bin forward/reverse pair has exactly the same binned ledger and a positive order-\(\delta\) target gap under \(\beta_*<\Lambda_Y\). On the regular binary-bin class, minimax risk and honest expected length have order \(n^{-1/2}\vee\delta\), with crossover at \(\sqrt n\,\delta\asymp1\). Without reset, a persistent-timestamp pair belongs to the causally valid two-process event-history class on every admissible grid and forces a fixed positive minimax risk and honest-length floor under ledger observation.
gap: Full-trajectory continuous-time identification results and linear discretization analyses do not characterize the suppression-mean fiber when both treatment and outcome event times are reduced to bin counts.
fill: Establish a canonical modular clock model, conditional path tilt and uniform mesh radius, exact same-ledger reset and nonreset witnesses, and feasible rate-matched inference on a binary-bin regular subclass.
